signals.name: Leopold Aschenbrenner
signals.summary: Mid-September reports describe Aschenbrenner's fund Situational Awareness re-entering the market via options bets on AI stocks, after unwinding public positions in July following steep losses.
signals.connection: Underscores volatility and leverage building up around AI-linked equities as bond yields climb and a Fed hike is priced in.

signals.name: Nathan Benaich
signals.summary: Previewed the State of AI Report 2026 ahead of an October 8 SF launch and amplified a claim from Jakub Pachocki that current AI progress could sustain into recursive self-improvement, with near-term capability jumps of equal or larger magnitude.
signals.connection: Feeds directly into Frontier Tech/AI and AI Regulation & Governance, echoing the caution behind OpenAI's sandbox-escape training halt.

signals.name: Stanley Druckenmiller
signals.summary: Described a global 'war for capital' as tech giants' infrastructure buildouts compete with government borrowing, and said he's cut AI-related positions to roughly 20% of where they stood six months ago, citing earnings-bubble risk.
signals.connection: Directly relevant to today's bond-yield spike and priced-in Fed hike, and to broader AI-bubble market concerns.

signals.name: Byrne Hobart
signals.summary: September 23 post pushed back on commentary around the Charlie Kirk-adjacent assassination debate, arguing people rarely say which political views they'd abandon if a proponent were killed.

signals.name: Ben Thompson
signals.summary: Weekly roundup plus standalone pieces covering Meta vs. Amazon over Muse, GM capitulating to Apple CarPlay, an interview on profiling Mark Zuckerberg, and whether Google is being squeezed out of the platform fight.
signals.connection: Core Applied Tech & Industry read on aggregator power struggles reshaping platform competition in the AI era.

signals.name: Paul Graham
signals.summary: Defended Elon Musk's stewardship of X, noting the press had wrongly predicted the platform would collapse after his takeover.

signals.name: Benedict Evans
signals.summary: Remains off X/Twitter (moved to Threads); published an essay in early September on AI, tools, and transformation on his personal site.
signals.connection: Background context for how AI tools are reshaping work, adjacent to today's Frontier Tech/AI and Labor & Workforce threads.

signals.name: Packy McCormick
signals.summary: Roundup covering Vironexis, Solcoa, Terraform, Joby, and Meta's VR glasses, alongside a separate piece on what an AI-native school (HAA) would look like.
signals.connection: Touches Applied Tech & Industry and Energy via the startup roundup (Terraform, Joby).

signals.name: Lenny Rachitsky
signals.latest_title: The grief, loneliness, and burnout sweeping through the tech industry right now | Molly Graham
signals.summary: Interviewed Molly Graham on burnout, grief, and delegating to AI vs. humans, alongside a Community Wisdom roundup and a blind test pitting Opus 5.5 against GPT-6 Sol on coding and writing tasks.
signals.connection: Speaks to Labor & Workforce strain from AI adoption and frontier-model competition (Opus 5.5 vs. GPT-6 Sol).

signals.name: Andrej Karpathy
signals.summary: Endorsed Dario Amodei's essay arguing the AI industry should slow down, saying he hopes the industry can 'come together' on it; separately discussed a Sequoia Ascent fireside on LLMs enabling new categories of bespoke software.
signals.connection: Directly connects to AI Regulation & Governance and the frontier-safety debate underscored by OpenAI's sandbox-escape training halt.
